title: A positive line power satisfies the square condition on a smooth action with connected generic fibre
statement: Let $D$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension at most one, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and put $K=\operatorname{Frac}D$. Let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme of finite type with geometrically connected fibres [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A group scheme has multiplication, inverse and identity satisfying the group identities (the relative version of [def-sc-group-scheme]); separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $X\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type, with an action $a:H\times_SX\to X$ satisfying unit and associativity [def-pc-fibre-product], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Assume the generic fibre $X_K=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$ is nonempty and geometrically connected, meaning that it stays connected after every extension of $K$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there is an integer $r\geq1$ such that $M=L^{\otimes r}$ satisfies the square condition for this action. For any $S$-scheme $B$, write $X_B=X\times_SB$, $q_B:X_B\to B$, and $M_B$ for tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $g\in H(B)$ let $\tau_g$ be translation by $g$ on $X_B$. Say that an invertible module $M$ satisfies the square condition if for every $B$ and $g,h\in H(B)$ there is an invertible module $N$ on $B$ and an isomorphism $$\tau_{gh}^*M_B\otimes M_B\cong\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B\otimes q_B^*N,$$ with sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. No chosen isomorphisms or coherence data are required.

source.place: BLR 6.3 Theorem 1, printed p.149 (PDF p.155), together with the functorial square-condition definition on printed pp.148–149 (PDF pp.154–155). Affine integral dimension-at-most-one specialization, with extra separatedness hypotheses; field case included. Local PDF WANTED; online primary scan read.

proof.text: The base $S$ is regular. Indeed each $D_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian and integrally closed: ideals localize their finite generators, and if $z$ is integral over a localization, multiplying $z$ by a common denominator in its monic equation makes it integral over $D$. Its dimension is at most one by the prime correspondence. A zero-dimensional local domain is a field, hence regular; in dimension one apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal]. Set $T=H\times_SH$, $Y=T\times_SX$, and denote their projections by $t:T\to S$, $f:Y\to T$, $p:Y\to X$, and $q:X\to S$. Base change of smoothness [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and composition [lem-trf-smooth-composition] show that $T,Y$ are smooth over $S$. The affine-local smooth-ring interpretation in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-smooth-ascent] make $H,X,T,Y$ regular. All are locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] and quasi-compact by finite type over the affine Noetherian base; hence Noetherian. Each smooth separated finite-type morphism here is of finite presentation: it is locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact, and its closed diagonal is quasi-compact. These are precisely the three conditions in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), (3) iff (5); Tag 07NF (lemma-regular-goes-up). BLR 6.3 Lemma 2, regularity of the products.

proof.text: For any $s\in S$ and any field extension $F/\kappa(s)$, the scheme $H_F$ is nonempty (identity section) and is normal and integral by [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality]. Applied to $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, the same node makes $X_K$ geometrically integral. Also $H_F\times_FH_F$ is integral: apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] to its projection onto the normal integral scheme $H_F$. This projection is smooth by base change and all its fibres are geometrically connected base changes of $H_F$. Now $X$ is normal by [rem-pc-regular-normal](1), and its finitely many irreducible components are disjoint open and closed by clause (2). Every nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$ meets $X_K$: smoothness is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], so [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain] makes $A\to A\otimes_DK$ injective; its nonzero target has a prime. Thus every component meets $X_K$. Since $X_K$ is integral, only one component is possible. Consequently $X$ is normal integral, its generic point maps to the generic point of $S$, and $X_K$ is dense. In particular this argument imposes no connectedness or nonemptiness requirement on the special fibres of $X$.

source.place: Tag 057J (lemma-normal-morphism-irreducible), smooth geometric-fibre specialization; properties.tex Tag 033M. BLR 6.3 Lemma 2, integral-base reduction.

proof.text: On $H\times_SH\times_SX$ define $b(u,v,x)=(uv^{-1})x$ and $A=b^*L$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-product-square-power] over $K$ to the three factors $H_K,H_K,X_K$ and the line $A_K$. Their geometric integrality is Step 2; smoothness, separatedness and finite presentation survive base change by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). We obtain $r\geq1$ and a line $J_K$ on $H_K^4$ such that $D(A_K^{\otimes r})\cong\pi_K^*J_K$, with $D$ and $\pi_K$ exactly as in the cited node. Put $M=L^{\otimes r}$. Pullbacks preserve lines, duals and tensor products: on a local frame the tensor pullback of [def-pc-module-pullback] sends its generator to $1\otimes e$, so these assertions follow by multiplying generators [def-sc-invertible-module]. Thus $A_K^{\otimes r}=b_K^*M_K$.

source.place: Proposition 5.2(ii), field case, printed pp.11-12; March 31, 2026 author PDF read online. BLR 6.3 Theorem 1, final field reduction.

proof.text: Define maps $c_{12},c_1,c_2:Y\to X$ by $c_{12}(g,h,x)=(gh)x$, $c_1(g,h,x)=gx$, $c_2(g,h,x)=hx$, and define the line $$C=c_{12}^*M\otimes p^*M\otimes(c_1^*M)^{-1}\otimes(c_2^*M)^{-1}.$$ Pull the isomorphism of Step 3 back along $$Y_K\longrightarrow H_K^4\times_KX_K,\qquad(g,h,x)\longmapsto(g,e,h^{-1},e,x).$$ In the order $(r_{00},r_{11},r_{01},r_{10})$ of the field-product node, the four composites with $b_K$ are $(gh)x,x,gx,hx$. Therefore $$C_K\cong f_K^*N_K,\qquad N_K=(g,h\mapsto(g,e,h^{-1},e))^*J_K.$$ Pullback composition is the formula of [def-pc-module-pullback], and cancellation of lines uses [def-sc-invertible-module]. No factors of $H$ have been commuted.

source.place: 6.3, printed p.149 (PDF p.155), universal square-difference line; the coordinate specialization supplies its generic descent line.

proof.text: Extend $N_K$ to a line $N$ on $T$. Here are the two separate extension inputs. Index by the small directed set of finite subsets $E\subset D\setminus\{0\}$ and set $d_E=\prod_{a\in E}a$, $T_E=T\times_SD(d_E)$. Each $T_E$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, by the finite-presentation and separated base-change clauses used in Step 3. Transition maps are affine: on any affine chart they are localization at the additional base elements. Their inverse limit is $T_K$, since a morphism to $T$ factors through every $T_E$ exactly when all nonzero elements of $D$ become units, equivalently when its base map factors through $\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [lem-trf-invertible-affine-limit-descent], $N_K$ descends to a line on some open $T_E$. Every local ring of $T$ is regular by Step 1, hence a UFD by [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] with the empty parameter tuple. Apply [lem-sfb-invertible-extension-factorial-complement] to $T_E\subseteq T$ to obtain $N$ extending that line, with $N|_{T_K}\cong N_K$. In the field case one can take $T_E=T$.

source.place: Tag 0B8W (lemma-descend-invertible-modules), (2); divisors.tex Tag 0BD9 (lemma-extend-invertible-module); more-algebra.tex Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD). BLR 6.3 Lemma 2, extension of the generic base line.

proof.text: Put $R=C\otimes(f^*N)^{-1}$ on $Y$. Step 4 gives $R|_{Y_K}\cong\mathcal O_{Y_K}$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-noetherian-generic-line-pullback] to $p:Y\to X$ and $R$. Its hypotheses hold as follows: $X$ is normal integral by Step 2; $X,Y$ are Noetherian by Step 1; $p$ is smooth, hence flat and locally of finite type, by base change and [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. For any $x\in X$ mapping to $s\in S$, its fibre is $H_{\kappa(x)}\times_{\kappa(x)}H_{\kappa(x)}$, integral and nonempty by Step 2, applied to $\kappa(x)/\kappa(s)$. Finally the generic point of $X$ lies in $X_K$, so $R$ is trivial on the generic fibre of $p$, by restriction of its trivialization on $Y_K$. The cited node therefore gives a line $P$ on $X$ and $R\cong p^*P$. This uses the projection to $X$, whose fibres are integral, rather than the projection to $T$, whose fibres need not be integral.

source.place: Tag 0BD7 (lemma-in-image-pullback), all hypotheses (1)-(5). BLR 6.3 Lemma 2, projection onto X in the vertical-divisor argument.

proof.text: Let $e_2:S\to T$ be $(e,e)$ and let $\sigma:X\to Y$ be $x\mapsto(e,e,x)$. The action unit identity gives $\sigma^*C\cong M\otimes M\otimes M^{-1}\otimes M^{-1}\cong\mathcal O_X$. Also $p\sigma=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $f\sigma=e_2q$. Pulling $R\cong p^*P$ back along $\sigma$ thus gives $$P\cong q^*(e_2^*N)^{-1}.$$ Since $qp=tf$, substitution into $C\cong f^*N\otimes p^*P$ yields $$C\cong f^*N_0,\qquad N_0=N\otimes t^*(e_2^*N)^{-1}.$$ These equalities use only pullback composition and the local-frame tensor and dual formulas [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: 6.3 Lemma 2, printed p.151 (PDF p.157), pullback along the pair of identity sections; normalized correction of the base line.

proof.text: For any $S$-scheme $B$ and $g,h\in H(B)$, pull $C\cong f^*N_0$ back along $$X_B\longrightarrow Y,\qquad x\longmapsto(g,h,x).$$ Its four left factors become $\tau_{gh}^*M_B,M_B,(\tau_g^*M_B)^{-1},(\tau_h^*M_B)^{-1}$; its right side becomes $q_B^*(g,h)^*N_0$. Tensor both sides with $\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B$ and cancel inverse lines [def-sc-invertible-module]. This is exactly the required square condition, with base line $(g,h)^*N_0$ and the single exponent $r$ from Step 3. The computation uses tensor pullback and its composition law [def-pc-module-pullback]; it is valid for nonreduced, disconnected or empty $B$ as well as for field-valued points.

Step 2 uses clauses (1) and (2), regular implies normal and disjoint integral components of a Noetherian normal scheme.
